title: The reactor OpenTelemetry package only creates instruments on the global meter and reads no environment variables, so a host that configures no exporter gets no metrics
content:
`@powerhousedao/opentelemetry-instrumentation-reactor` inspects `ReactorModule` dependencies and subscribes to reactor event-bus events to register instruments covering the job queue, executor, read-model indexing and sync subsystems.

Its scope is deliberately narrow: it **only creates OTel instruments on the global meter** and does **not** configure exporters or collector endpoints. The taxonomy states the same rule from the other side — the package itself reads **no environment variables**; all configuration belongs to the host's OTel bootstrap.

```ts
const instrumentation = new ReactorInstrumentation(module); // module from ReactorBuilder
instrumentation.start();  // subscribe + register observable gauge callbacks
instrumentation.stop();   // remove all subscriptions, clear internal state
```

Metrics are recorded on the `@powerhousedao/reactor` meter via the global `@opentelemetry/api` `metrics.getMeter()`, so to see anything the application must configure a `MeterProvider` with an exporter in its entry point. The peer dependency is `@powerhousedao/reactor`.

The consequence for debugging: "no reactor metrics" has two very different causes — the instrumentation was never `start()`ed, or the host never wired a `MeterProvider`. The standard SDK variables a host typically sets are `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` (metrics export is disabled when unset) and `OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL` (default 60000 ms).
